oil.summary: Crude collapsed on Wednesday, with WTI shedding 4.56% to $69.87/bbl and Brent off 5.06% to $73.18, extending a brutal monthly drawdown of roughly 27-29%. The dominant driver is the U.S.-Iran détente: Washington granted a 60-day sanctions waiver through 21 August, with Treasury formally waiving restrictions and nuclear inspectors set to return, unlocking Persian Gulf barrels for India and global buyers. VLCC day-rates reportedly surged near $470,000 as charterers scrambled for tonnage, a sign physical demand for Iranian crude is real. Bears were reinforced by China's crude imports plunging to their lowest since 2018, crimping the demand side. A 6.1-million-barrel U.S. inventory draw and CME options pricing a 77% probability of an OPEC cut at the next meeting provided modest offsets but failed to stem the selloff. Rosneft's Sechin separately proposed a 30% domestic-refining mandate to address Russia's fuel crunch.
drivers: U.S. 60-day Iran sanctions waiver unlocks fresh Persian Gulf supply, reversing the Hormuz risk premium
China crude imports hit lowest level since 2018, undermining the demand outlook
OPEC options market prices 77% probability of a production cut, but has not yet arrested the slide; U.S. stocks drew 6.1 mb

gas.summary: Henry Hub edged up 3.72% to $3.264/MMBtu, extending a 12% monthly gain, while European TTF eased 2.06% to €41.15/MWh — now down 15% on the month. The divergence likely reflects U.S. domestic tightness contrasting with European relief as Iran-related supply risk fades and LNG flows normalise. Headline flow for gas-specific catalysts is thin today; the only proximate headlines concern Russian seaborne fuel-oil and VGO export declines of 6% in May due to Ukrainian strikes, and the Iran sanctions waiver which may free up some associated gas and LNG volumes. Traders should note the data gap and treat today's Henry Hub move cautiously until storage or weather data clarifies.
drivers: Henry Hub +3.72% on the day, supported by ongoing U.S. domestic tightness and a +12% monthly trend
TTF -2.06% on the day and -15% over one month as Iran-deal optimism eases European supply-risk premium
Gas-specific headline flow is sparse today; Russian seaborne fuel-oil/VGO exports fell 6% in May due to Ukraine strikes, a marginal supply signal

power.summary: EU Carbon EUAs held nearly flat at $76.45/EUA (-0.16%), supported by a positive one-month trend (+3.56%) even as TTF continued to soften. The macro backdrop for carbon is shaped by falling gas prices pressuring fuel-switching economics, partially offset by structural power-demand optimism. The standout thematic today is nuclear: Canada broke ground on the Western world's first grid-scale SMR; Trump's nuclear push is framed as a response to an estimated $800 billion in U.S. data-centre capex this year alone; and India's Adani Group targeted 10 GW of nuclear capacity by 2035. On the geopolitical side, the UK joined eight North Sea nations on a clean-energy offshore initiative, and the euro sank to a one-year low as cheaper oil fuelled ECB rate-cut expectations, an indirect headwind for EUA demand via lower industrial output assumptions.
drivers: Nuclear buildout accelerating on multiple fronts: Canada's first grid-scale SMR under construction, U.S. nuclear push tied to $800bn data-centre capex, Adani targeting 10 GW in India by 2035
EU EUAs broadly stable (+3.56% monthly) despite TTF softness; falling gas prices compress fuel-switching support for carbon
UK and eight North Sea partners launch clean-energy offshore initiative; weaker euro on oil-drop/ECB cut bets signals softer near-term industrial demand
